## Overview

This is a chart built around one strong, talkative, slightly restless main star in the Life Palace, with the Body Palace placed some distance from it. The Life Palace sits in the Xu 戌 branch and holds Ju Men (fallen) — Ju Men is the orator and debater, the star of speech, persuasion and argument. "Fallen" brightness means its gift tends to come out sideways: opinions that arrive faster than the situation calls for, sharp observation that lands harder than intended, plenty of inner commentary. Read positively, it is a mind that can take anything apart and explain it well when it has an audience and a purpose. The Body Palace sits in the Travel Palace, which is where a person's physical life and later-life momentum gather; here it holds Tian Tong (neutral) with birth-year Hua Lu (prosperity). Tian Tong is the easygoing, comfort-loving star, the one who prefers harmony over friction. So the inner design is: a quick, critical mind, carried by a body and daily life that wants things pleasant, mobile and unhurried.

The Five Element Bureau is Wood 3, which sets the rhythm of the Major Periods and gives the chart a growing, branching quality — progress that comes in stages rather than in one leap. Two traits stand out. First, a real skill with words and ideas that needs a constructive channel; without one, it turns into self-talk or argument. Second, a life that is happiest in motion — the Body Palace in Travel with Hua Lu there suggests that changing place, learning through going somewhere, and staying flexible is where ease and opportunity come from.

For a newcomer: the twelve palaces are like twelve rooms of a house, and the chart places stars in each. The Life Palace is the room of self — temperament, instinct, the way you meet the world. The Body Palace is the room of lived, physical life — where your energy actually goes, and what matters to you in the second half of life. They are read together, and here they pull in two different directions, which is the interesting part.

## Life Palace and Personality

The Life Palace holds Ju Men (fallen) alone, with no supporting stars. Ju Men is speech, analysis, debate and the pleasure of a well-made argument. In fallen brightness, the tendency is toward verbal speed and mental restlessness: you may spot the flaw in a plan before anyone has finished describing it, or replay conversations afterwards wishing you had said something differently. Its supporting-star absence means there is nothing to soften or distract — the Ju Men quality is the whole flavour of the palace, so it shows up strongly. The opposite palace is the Travel Palace, holding Tian Tong (neutral), so the relaxed, sociable side of you is what people actually meet in daily life, while the debating mind works away underneath.

A useful way to work with this: give Ju Men a job. Writing, teaching, editing, negotiating, explaining, translating, mediating, any role where precision with language is the point. When Ju Men has an outlet, its critical energy becomes craft. When it has none, it tends to turn on the nearest person, including yourself. A simple habit helps — before voicing a correction, ask whether it needs to be said now, and whether it needs to be said by you.

## Career

The Career Palace is in the Yin 寅 branch and is empty; it borrows Tian Ji (steady) and Tai Yin (fair) from the opposite Spouse Palace. It also holds Di Jie (challenging). Tian Ji is the strategist and problem-solver, the star of plans, adjustments and clever workarounds; Tai Yin is the gentle, detail-loving, aesthetic and caring star. Borrowed into the career room, this points to work that rewards planning, resourcefulness and a quiet, thorough style rather than loud ambition — analysis, design, research, planning, editing, advisory roles, or anything with a caretaking or aesthetic dimension. Di Jie as a challenging star suggests the career path may not be a straight line: sudden changes of direction, a role that ends abruptly and opens something better, or a plan that needs reworking mid-way. Treat it as pressure that keeps you adaptable rather than a warning.

The Parents Palace holds Tian Xiang (steady) with You Bi and Tian Kui, both auspicious, which is a supportive sign for mentors, seniors and the people who open doors for you — worth using actively. Asking for introductions and staying in touch with older, more established contacts is well suited to this chart. The Friends Palace is empty but borrows Zi Wei (bright) and Tan Lang (fair) and holds Zuo Fu (auspicious), which suggests that collaborators and networks bring real strength — Zi Wei is the dignified leader, Tan Lang the charming, ambitious networker. Partnership and referral tend to work better for you than going entirely alone.

## Wealth

The Wealth Palace holds Tai Yang (bright) — the sun, the star of visibility, generosity and public-facing energy. Bright Tai Yang is a genuinely good placement for earning through being seen and known: reputation, visibility, being the person others recommend. It also carries Qing Yang and Ling Xing, both challenging stars. Qing Yang is a sharp, thrusting energy and Ling Xing an impatient, sparking one; together they suggest money comes in with a certain force and urgency, and can leave the same way. The practical reading is that income tends to be active and earned rather than passive, and that sudden impulses to spend or commit deserve a pause.

The opposite palace is the Spirit Palace with Tian Liang (brilliant) — Tian Liang is the elder, the advisor who stabilizes and shelters. That is a helpful counterweight: your sense of inner contentment is your financial anchor. When decisions feel urgent, going back to what actually makes you feel secure tends to sort out the noise. A standing habit of reviewing spending on a fixed day, rather than reacting to the moment, suits Qing Yang and Ling Xing well. This reading offers no financial advice; it only describes tendencies.

## Love and Partnership

The Spouse Palace holds Tian Ji (steady) with birth-year Hua Quan (power) and Tai Yin (fair), plus Di Kong (challenging). Tian Ji in this palace points to a partner who is clever, thoughtful and adaptable — someone who thinks things through and likes solving problems together. Hua Quan gives Tian Ji extra force: the partner, or the relationship itself, may carry a strong drive to direct and decide. That can be attractive and it can also mean two strong opinions in one room; with Ju Men in your Life Palace, negotiation is a natural theme. Tai Yin softens the picture and suggests warmth, attentiveness and a domestic, caring streak in the bond. Di Kong as a challenging star suggests periods of distance or a sense of something not fully expressed — worth naming early rather than letting it sit.

Since the Career Palace borrows Tian Ji and Tai Yin from here, work and partnership are linked in your chart: a supportive home base tends to steady your working life, and a chaotic work life tends to spill over. Choosing someone who respects your need for verbal space, and who can disagree without it becoming a contest, is well suited to this configuration.

## Wellbeing Habits

The Health Palace holds Wu Qu (neutral) and Po Jun (neutral) — Wu Qu is the steady, disciplined, physical star, and Po Jun is the pioneer who clears the old to build the new. Together they suggest a body that responds well to routine and structure (Wu Qu) but also goes through phases of wanting to change everything at once (Po Jun). The Life Palace's Ju Men adds a mental, verbal restlessness that can keep the system running hot. The opposite palace is the Parents Palace with Tian Xiang (steady), a stabilizing influence on health matters.

In practice: sleep tends to benefit from a fixed wind-down and from getting the day's unfinished conversations out of your head before bed — writing them down suits Ju Men. Food-wise, Po Jun suggests you may swing between strict phases and careless ones; a moderate, unremarkable routine is more useful than dramatic resets. Movement suits Wu Qu's nature: something regular and physical, done at the same time most days, rather than sporadic bursts. For emotional balance, Ju Men needs to talk and Tian Tong in the Travel Palace needs to move — a walk with a friend covers both. If you feel unwell, please consult a qualified healthcare professional.

## Family and Social Circle

The Parents Palace holds Tian Xiang (steady) with You Bi and Tian Kui, both auspicious — a supportive signature for parents, elders and mentors. Tian Xiang is the ministerial star, loyal and steady, and the two auspicious helpers suggest that guidance and backing from older figures is available to you when you ask. The Siblings Palace holds Zi Wei (bright) and Tan Lang (fair) with Tian Yue (auspicious) — Zi Wei is the dignified, self-possessed leader and Tan Lang the charming, ambitious social star. Siblings or close peers may be strong personalities, capable and a bit proud, and Tian Yue points to genuine warmth and help flowing between you.

The Friends Palace is empty and borrows Zi Wei (bright) and Tan Lang (fair) from the Siblings Palace; it holds Zuo Fu (auspicious), the helper star that supports quietly. Your wider circle tends to mirror your close peers: capable, sociable, useful. The Children Palace holds Tian Fu (brilliant) — Tian Fu is the treasure-keeper, stable and resourceful — with Wen Chang carrying birth-year Hua Ke (recognition) and Wen Qu, both auspicious. That is a strongly literary, studious signature for children or creative projects: learning, writing and recognition tend to feature.

## Major Period and Year by Year

The Current Major Period runs in the Property Palace, Xin Chou 辛丑, East Asian ages 33–42 (about 2018–2027), holding Lian Zhen (fair) with birth-year Hua Ji (obstacle, needs extra care) and Qi Sha (brilliant). Lian Zhen is the star of principle, propriety and controlled ambition; Qi Sha is the decisive, forceful general. This is a ten-year stretch with a serious, driving tone — a period for consolidating foundations, property and structure, and for making firm decisions. The Hua Ji on Lian Zhen is the note to watch: it suggests friction around rules, boundaries and obligations, and a tendency to over-tighten. The pace is steady but pressured; the productive move is to keep standards high without making them rigid.

The Next Major Period moves to the Career Palace, Geng Yin 庚寅, East Asian ages 43–52 (about 2028–2037), an empty palace borrowing Tian Ji (steady) and Tai Yin (fair) from the Spouse Palace. The direction shifts from forceful consolidation toward strategy, planning and gentler, more collaborative work — a quieter but more thoughtful decade.

Each annual pillar follows the Chinese lunar year and roughly matches the calendar year.

### 2026 丙午 · Bing Wu

The annual Life Palace falls on the natal Wealth Palace, Tai Yang (bright) — a visible, outward-facing year where reputation and being seen carry weight. The year's Hua Lu lands on Tian Tong in the natal Travel Palace, which favours movement, travel, learning through going somewhere, and ease in day-to-day life; Hua Quan on Tian Ji in the natal Spouse Palace puts drive and decision-making into partnership and close one-to-one dealings; Hua Ke on Wen Chang in the natal Children Palace supports study, writing and creative or family projects that need recognition. Hua Ji on Lian Zhen in the natal Property Palace is where care is needed — rules, obligations and property matters benefit from patience and a slower pace, especially in the first half of the year.

Combined with the Property Palace Major Period, this is a year of outward visibility resting on a structured base. Lean into travel, learning and partner conversations; keep property and administrative matters unhurried and reviewed twice. Early in the year is a good time to plan rather than force.

### 2027 丁未 · Ding Wei

The annual Life Palace moves to the natal Children Palace, Tian Fu (brilliant), with Wen Chang carrying Hua Ke and Wen Qu — a year oriented toward creative output, study, and the younger generation or projects you are raising. Hua Lu on Tai Yin in the natal Spouse Palace brings warmth and emotional ease into partnership; Hua Quan on Tian Tong in the natal Travel Palace gives momentum to travel and social ease; Hua Ke on Tian Ji in the natal Spouse Palace highlights thoughtful, well-recognized problem-solving with a partner. Hua Ji on Ju Men in the natal Life Palace is the year's tender spot: watch for words landing harder than intended, and for over-arguing.

With Tian Fu's steady, resourceful quality, this tends to be a good year for finishing things — a course, a manuscript, a family project. In the second half, when conversation gets heated, pausing before replying does a lot of work.

### 2028 戊申 · Wu Shen

A new Major Period begins this year: the Career Palace, Geng Yin 庚寅, ages 43–52. The annual Life Palace falls on the natal Spouse Palace, Tian Ji (steady) and Tai Yin (fair) — partnership and close relationships are the year's centre of gravity. Hua Lu on Tan Lang in the natal Siblings Palace brings charm and opportunity through peers and siblings; Hua Quan on Tai Yin in the natal Spouse Palace gives emotional matters drive and direction; Hua Ke on You Bi in the natal Parents Palace highlights support from elders and mentors. Hua Ji on Tian Ji in the natal Spouse Palace is the place for care — the same palace that sets the year's tone, so negotiations with a partner deserve extra patience and clarity.

Entering a ten-year period that borrows Tian Ji and Tai Yin, this year sets the pattern: strategy, collaboration and steady planning. Lean into partnership conversations and mentor relationships; keep expectations explicit rather than assumed.

### 2029 己酉 · Ji You

The annual Life Palace falls on the natal Siblings Palace, Zi Wei (bright) and Tan Lang (fair) — a socially strong year, with peers, siblings and networks prominent and confident energy around you. Hua Lu on Wu Qu in the natal Health Palace favours routine-building and physical steadiness; Hua Quan on Tan Lang in the natal Siblings Palace gives social initiatives real push; Hua Ke on Tian Liang in the natal Spirit Palace supports inner calm and recognition for your steadier, advisory side. Hua Ji on Wen Qu in the natal Children Palace is the watch point — creative or study projects may need extra care, and details in writing and paperwork are worth slowing down for.

With the Career Palace Major Period, this is a year where your network does the heavy lifting. Toward the end of the year, review the small print on anything creative you've committed to.

### 2030 庚戌 · Geng Xu

The annual Life Palace returns to your natal Life Palace, Ju Men (fallen) — a year where your own voice, opinions and communication style take centre stage. Hua Lu on Tai Yang in the natal Wealth Palace gives visibility and outward momentum, a good time to be seen and to present your work; Hua Quan on Wu Qu in the natal Health Palace supports discipline and steady habits; Hua Ke on Tai Yin in the natal Spouse Palace brings warmth and recognition in partnership. Hua Ji on Tian Tong in the natal Travel Palace is where to go gently — travel plans and ease of daily life may need extra margin and flexibility.

This year rewards communication and punishes carelessness with words, so it suits presenting, teaching, writing and public-facing work. In the second half, plan travel with room to adjust, and keep the debating instinct pointed at problems rather than people.

## Guidance

- Give Ju Men in the Life Palace a deliberate outlet: writing, teaching, editing or negotiating. When the debating mind has a task, it stops turning on the people around you.
- Because the Career Palace borrows Tian Ji and Tai Yin and holds Di Jie, build in review points rather than one fixed long-term plan — expect the path to bend, and keep skills portable.
- Use the Parents Palace's You Bi and Tian Kui actively: ask older contacts and mentors for introductions, and stay in touch with them as a matter of habit.
- With Qing Yang and Ling Xing in the Wealth Palace, set a fixed day to review spending and to wait a set period before any large purchase. The aim is a pause, not a rule.
- Lean into the Travel Palace's Tian Tong with Hua Lu: regular changes of scene, short trips and a mobile routine suit the Body Palace, and tend to refresh both mood and perspective.
